requirement: Children's products shall not contain lead in accessible component substrate materials exceeding 100 ppm (0.01%).
requirement_summary: Kids product substrate lead content must be ≤100 ppm

evidence_required.description: Third-party lab lead content test report (XRF or chemical analysis) showing substrate lead ≤100 ppm

remediation: Replace or reformulate substrate materials to ensure lead content does not exceed 100 ppm per CPSIA Section 101(a).

requirement: Children's products shall not contain paint or surface coatings with lead content exceeding 90 ppm (0.009%).
requirement_summary: Kids product paint/coating lead content must be ≤90 ppm

evidence_required.description: Third-party lab coating lead content test report showing paint/surface coating lead ≤90 ppm

remediation: Replace or reformulate paint and surface coatings to ensure lead content does not exceed 90 ppm per CPSIA Section 101(f).

requirement: Children's toys or child care articles containing plasticized components that can be placed in the mouth shall not contain more than 0.1% of each of the six specified phthalates: DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DnOP, DIDP.
requirement_summary: Kids product mouthable plastic parts must have each of 6 phthalates ≤0.1%

evidence_required.description: Third-party lab phthalates test report (GC-MS) showing each of 6 phthalates ≤0.1%

remediation: Replace plasticized components that can be placed in the mouth with phthalate-free alternatives, ensuring each of DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DnOP, DIDP does not exceed 0.1% per CPSIA Section 108.

requirement: Products intended for children under 3 years of age shall not contain detachable small parts that can pass through the 16 CFR 1501 small parts cylinder test, to prevent swallowing and choking hazards.
requirement_summary: Products for children <3 must not have detachable small parts (16 CFR 1501 cylinder test)

evidence_required.description: Small parts test report per 16 CFR 1501 cylinder test showing no detachable small parts

remediation: Eliminate or secure all small detachable parts that could pass through the 16 CFR 1501 small parts cylinder to prevent choking hazards for children under 3.
